albania republic of albania tirana closed to the world until 1991, and now the least developed and least expensive coast on the mediterranean. albania spent forty years as the most isolated country in europe, and the 173,000 concrete bunkers built during it are still in the fields. since opening it has become the balkans' fastest-changing destination: an ionian coast with genuinely empty beaches, an alpine north with a working blood-feud memory and hospitality codes older than the state, and a capital painted in primary colours. coast mountains history food nature
tirana, the riviera & the south the painted capital, two ottoman museum-towns, and the ionian coast. coast history food architecture

bunk'art, underground a five-storey bunker built for a leadership expecting invasion that never came; the exhibition does not soften the regime. museum

theth a valley village of stone houses with no road in until recently, a lock-in tower, and a waterfall above it. the valbona-theth pass, a six-hour crossing on foot the kulla, a tower where men under blood feud could shelter the blue eye of theth, up the river mountains nature history albania the albanian alps
the valbona to theth pass six to eight hours over 1,800 metres between two valleys, with guesthouses at both ends and mules for bags. walk
the koman lake ferry three hours through a flooded gorge on a working passenger boat that carries villagers, goats and the occasional car. water

andorra principality of andorra andorra la vella a pyrenean co-principality with two heads of state, no airport, and the highest capital in europe. andorra is 468 square kilometres of pyrenean valley, jointly headed by the president of france and a spanish bishop — an arrangement running since 1278. catalan is the official language. it is best known for duty-free shopping and skiing, and least known for romanesque chapels and a genuinely wild high valley on the unesco list. mountains winter nature sacred
the valleys the capital in the deepest valley, ski country above, and a roadless unesco valley to the southeast. mountains winter nature sacred

andorra la vella europe's highest capital at 1,023 metres, in a narrow valley, mostly shops with mountains directly behind them. casa de la vall, the 16th-century parliament house caldea thermal spa, fed by hot springs ski areas twenty minutes up the valley in either direction mountains winter andorra the valleys

madriu-perafita-claror a glacial valley with no road into it, on the unesco list for a cultural landscape of summer pasture and stone huts. nine per cent of the country, entered only on foot shepherds' bordes and dry-stone terraces still standing refuges with no booking and no warden mountains nature wild andorra the valleys
into the roadless valley six hours in from escaldes; the only sounds are water and cowbells, and the huts are open and free. walk

armenia republic of armenia yerevan the first state to adopt christianity, in 301, with monasteries in gorges and a mountain it can see but not reach. armenia is high, dry and volcanic, with an alphabet invented in 405 and a monastic architecture of grey tufa that sits in landscapes chosen for isolation. mount ararat dominates the skyline from yerevan and stands across the closed turkish border. the country is landlocked with two of its four borders shut, which shapes everything about how you get in and out. sacred history mountains food wine
yerevan & the ararat plain the pink tufa capital, the cathedral that founded a church, and the temple that predates it. sacred history food cities

yerevan a capital rebuilt in pink volcanic stone to a 1924 plan, with ararat filling the southern horizon. the cascade, a stairway of terraces and sculpture matenadaran, a library of 17,000 medieval manuscripts the vernissage market at weekends echmiadzin cathedral, from 301, twenty minutes west history food art cities armenia yerevan & the ararat plain
the manuscript library illuminated books rescued repeatedly over centuries, some buried during massacres and dug up afterwards. museum

garni & geghard a hellenistic temple on a gorge, and a monastery partly carved out of the rock face next door. garni: the only greco-roman colonnaded temple left in the former soviet union geghard's rock-cut chambers and their acoustics the basalt 'symphony of stones' columns in the gorge below history sacred nature armenia yerevan & the ararat plain
chant in a rock-cut chamber singers perform in the carved chambers because the acoustics are extraordinary; the sound arrives from the stone itself. sacred
the north & south forested monasteries in the north, lake sevan in the middle, and a cable car to a monastery in the south. sacred mountains nature wine

dilijan a forested spa town called 'armenian switzerland', with two of the country's finest monasteries in the woods nearby. haghartsin and goshavank monasteries in deep forest the transcaucasian trail through the national park lake sevan, thirty minutes away at 1,900 metres nature sacred mountains armenia the north & south

tatev a 9th-century monastery on a cliff in the far south, reached by the world's longest reversible cable car. the wings of tatev cable car, 5.7 km over a gorge the monastery's swinging pillar, an early seismograph the vorotan gorge below sacred mountains history armenia the north & south

austria republic of austria vienna an imperial capital with a small country attached, most of it vertical. austria spent six centuries as the seat of an empire and then lost it in an afternoon, which is why vienna is a capital built for twice the country. everything west of it is mountain: ski resorts in winter, high pasture in summer, and lakes cold enough to hurt. the coffee house, the opera and the sunday hike are all still institutions rather than attractions. music art mountains winter architecture food
vienna & the east the imperial capital, the danube valley's vineyards, and hungary's old border country. music art architecture wine cities

vienna habsburg on the outside, freud and klimt and social housing on the inside, with the world's best-funded music scene. klimt's kiss at the belvedere and the secession's beethoven frieze standing tickets at the staatsoper for the price of a sandwich the naschmarkt, and a coffee house afternoon with a newspaper on a stick red vienna's 1920s housing — karl-marx-hof is a kilometre long music art architecture food cities austria vienna & the east
standing room at the staatsoper a few euros, queued for on the night, in one of the great opera houses. bring a scarf to tie to the rail and hold your place. stage

dürnstein & the wachau a blue baroque tower over the danube, terraced vineyards behind, and the castle where richard the lionheart was held. grüner veltliner and riesling from terraces built by monks the danube cycle path, flat and shaded melk abbey upriver, gold from floor to ceiling wine nature history austria vienna & the east
salzburg & the salzkammergut a prince-archbishop's baroque city, and a district of seventy-six lakes behind it. music nature history mountains

salzburg baroque built on salt money, under a fortress, with mozart born in the middle of it. hohensalzburg fortress, never taken in a thousand years mozart's birthplace and the concerts in the residenz hellbrunn's trick fountains, designed in 1615 to soak guests music architecture history austria salzburg & the salzkammergut

hallstatt a lakeside village under a salt mountain, with 7,000 years of continuous mining and more visitors than it can hold. the oldest salt mine in the world, and a wooden staircase from 1344 inside it the bone house, with painted skulls stacked by family early morning or evening — the day-trip window is 10 to 4 and it is unbearable nature history austria salzburg & the salzkammergut
into the salt mountain miners' slides, a salt lake underground, and the bronze age tools that came out of the same shafts. museum
tyrol & the west the alpine heart: innsbruck between two ranges, and valleys of huts and high paths. mountains winter nature

innsbruck a university city at 574 metres with a 2,300-metre mountain reachable from the centre in twenty minutes. the nordkette funicular, zaha hadid stations from town to summit the golden roof and the old town beneath it ski jumping at bergisel, and the view from the tower mountains winter architecture cities austria tyrol & the west

azerbaijan republic of azerbaijan baku fire that comes out of the ground, a walled medieval city, and oil money spent on architecture. azerbaijan sits on the caspian, on gas reserves that have been burning at the surface for millennia — the zoroastrian fire temples were built around them. baku pairs a walled old city with a skyline of flame-shaped towers. beyond the capital the greater caucasus rises to 4,000 metres with mountain villages that kept their own languages, and mud volcanoes cover the semi-desert south. history architecture mountains food nature
baku & the caspian the walled city, the flame towers, the fire temple and the petroglyphs south of town. history architecture nature

baku a unesco-listed walled city with a mysterious stone tower, ringed by oil-boom mansions and three flame-shaped skyscrapers. icherisheher, the walled old city, and the maiden tower nobody can fully explain the heydar aliyev centre, zaha hadid's curved white building ateshgah, the fire temple, and yanar dag, a hillside that has burned for centuries gobustan's 6,000 petroglyphs and the mud volcanoes beside them architecture history food cities azerbaijan baku & the caspian
petroglyphs and mud volcanoes rock carvings of boats and dancers from 10,000 years ago, then a field of cold mud volcanoes burping methane a few kilometres on. walk
the northwest & the mountains sheki's caravanserai and stained glass, and villages high in the greater caucasus. history mountains food

sheki a silk road town under wooded mountains, with a khan's summer palace whose windows are built without glue or nails. the palace of sheki khans, with shebeke lattice windows of 5,000 pieces each the caravanserai, still taking guests sheki halva, layered and made only here history architecture food azerbaijan the northwest & the mountains
shebeke: glass without glue wooden lattice and coloured glass assembled entirely by friction; the workshops still make them and will show you the joints. workshop

xınalıq a village at 2,300 metres whose people speak a language related to nothing else, reached by a single mountain road. flat-roofed stone houses stacked up the slope the ketsh language, spoken by a few thousand people and nobody else shepherd routes into the high caucasus mountains nature history azerbaijan the northwest & the mountains

belarus republic of belarus minsk half forest, with the last primeval woodland in europe and a capital rebuilt entirely in stalinist stone. belarus is flat, forested and thinly populated, with the belarusian half of białowieża — the last primeval lowland forest on the continent — along its southwestern border. minsk was almost completely destroyed in the second world war and rebuilt as a planned socialist city, which makes it one of the most coherent examples of that architecture anywhere. nature wild history architecture
minsk & the centre the rebuilt capital and the castles west of it. architecture history

minsk a city rebuilt from almost nothing after 1944 along one monumental avenue, and unusually complete as a piece of urban design. independence avenue, 15 kilometres of stalinist ensemble the great patriotic war museum mir and nesvizh castles, both unesco-listed, west of the city architecture history cities belarus minsk & the centre
the forests the belarusian side of the primeval forest, and the lake district in the north. nature wild

belovezhskaya pushcha the belarusian half of europe's last primeval lowland forest, with bison and trees that have never been cut. european bison, reintroduced from captive stock after the species died out here oaks over 500 years old a unesco site shared across the polish border wild nature belarus the forests

belgium kingdom of belgium brussels three languages, six governments, the best beer in the world and a genuine talent for not explaining itself. belgium is small, divided and quietly excellent at the things that matter daily: bread, beer, chips, painting and comics. the medieval cloth towns of flanders — bruges, ghent, antwerp — got rich early and kept the buildings. brussels is the accidental capital of a continent and much better company than its reputation. food wine art architecture history cities
flanders the rich medieval north: cloth halls, belfries, flemish primitives and a port that runs on diamonds. art architecture history food

bruges a trading city frozen when its river silted up in the 1500s, which is why it looks like this. the belfry's 366 steps and the carillon at the top michelangelo's madonna, the only sculpture he sold abroad in his lifetime the city at seven in the morning, which is a different city architecture history art food belgium flanders
bruges before the coaches day-trippers arrive from ten. between six and nine the canals belong to you and the swans. walk

ghent bruges's rival, larger, younger and still a working student city rather than a museum of itself. the ghent altarpiece, restored, in the cathedral it was painted for the graslei quays at dusk vegetarian thursdays, a city policy since 2009 art history food music belgium flanders

antwerp rubens's city and the world's diamond exchange, with a fashion school that reset the industry in the 1980s. rubens's own house and studio the station, which is a cathedral pretending to be a station momu and the antwerp six's continuing influence art design food cities belgium flanders
brussels & wallonia the capital of europe, and the french-speaking south of forest, castle and old industry. art food history nature

brussels art nouveau streets, comic-strip walls, a gilded square, and the machinery of a continent in the eastern quarter. the grand-place, best at night when it is lit and empty horta's houses, four of them unesco-listed the comic strip route: fifty painted gables across the centre lambic breweries in anderlecht, fermenting on wild yeast art architecture food cities belgium brussels & wallonia
a lambic brewery, spontaneously fermented beer left open to the air of one valley, aged three years in barrel — the last place in the world doing this at scale. cellar

dinant a citadel on a cliff over the meuse, a bulbous cathedral below, and the birthplace of the saxophone. 408 steps or a cable car to the citadel kayaking the lesse down to the river adolphe sax's house, and saxophones on every bridge nature history music belgium brussels & wallonia

bosnia and herzegovina bosnia and herzegovina sarajevo where the ottoman and austro-hungarian worlds meet in one street, and the 1990s are still within touching distance. bosnia is mountainous, green and river-cut, with a capital where a mosque, a synagogue, an orthodox and a catholic church stand within a few hundred metres. the war of 1992–95 is visible in the buildings and unavoidable in conversation, and bosnians discuss it more openly than visitors expect. it is one of the cheapest and most hospitable countries in europe. history sacred mountains food nature
sarajevo & central bosnia the capital in its valley, the olympic mountains above, and the ottoman towns north of it. history sacred food mountains

the tunnel of hope 800 metres dug by hand under the runway; it kept the city alive for three years and is explained by people who used it. museum
bosnian coffee, properly džezva, fildžan, a sugar cube held in the teeth, and an hour of not being in a hurry. table

herzegovina the dry south: mostar's bridge, a dervish house at a spring, and karst rivers. history sacred nature wine

the bridge before the buses between six and nine the bazaar is a town rather than a market, and the bridge is a bridge. walk

blagaj a dervish monastery built against a cliff at the source of the buna, where a river comes out of a cave at full size. the tekke, a sufi lodge from around 1520, still in use the spring, one of europe's largest karst sources trout restaurants over the water below it sacred nature bosnia and herzegovina herzegovina

bulgaria republic of bulgaria sofia thracian gold, orthodox monasteries, rose fields and the cheapest good skiing in europe. bulgaria has been continuously inhabited since the neolithic and holds the oldest processed gold in the world, from a grave at varna. it is mountainous — two ranges cross it — with a black sea coast, a valley that supplies most of the world's rose oil, and a monastery tradition that kept the language alive under five centuries of ottoman rule. it is one of the best-value countries in the eu. sacred history mountains coast wine winter
sofia & the mountains the capital under a 2,290-metre peak, and the rila and pirin ranges south of it. sacred mountains history winter

sofia a capital with roman ruins under the metro stations and a mountain at the end of the tram line. alexander nevsky cathedral and its icon crypt the roman serdica ruins, excavated and left open in the middle of the city vitosha mountain, 2,290 metres, reached by public transport history sacred food cities bulgaria sofia & the mountains

rila monastery a fortified monastery in a forested valley, founded in the 10th century, with striped arcades and frescoes over every surface. the painted porch, with 1,200 scenes and no blank stone hrelyo's tower, from 1335, the only medieval part left staying overnight in a monastery cell after the day visitors leave sacred mountains history bulgaria sofia & the mountains

thrace & the black sea the rose valley, thracian tombs, an old-town on a hill, and the coast. history wine coast food

plovdiv one of europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities, on six hills, with a roman theatre still in use. the roman theatre, hosting opera and rock concerts since restoration the old town's 19th-century merchant houses with overhanging upper floors kapana, a craft district in the old artisans' quarter history art food architecture bulgaria thrace & the black sea

nessebar a rocky peninsula joined by a causeway, with more medieval churches per square metre than anywhere on the black sea. forty churches in a town of a few hundred metres across wooden ottoman-era houses on stone bases out of season, when it stops being a beach resort annexe history coast sacred bulgaria thrace & the black sea

croatia republic of croatia zagreb a thousand islands, a roman emperor's palace still lived in, and lakes that fall into each other. croatia is shaped like a pair of tongs around bosnia, with a long limestone coast and a flat continental interior that visitors skip. the adriatic islands — 1,244 of them, 48 inhabited — are the draw, along with two roman-founded cities that never stopped being used. it joined schengen and the euro in 2023, which changed the practicalities considerably. coast islands history nature food wine
dalmatia the southern coast: split's palace, dubrovnik's walls, and the islands between them. coast islands history food

split a roman emperor's retirement palace that became a town — people live inside the walls and always have. diocletian's palace, occupied continuously since 305 ad the riva at passeggiata hour marjan hill's pine woods and swimming coves, walkable from the centre ferries to hvar, brač and vis from the door history coast food cities croatia dalmatia
the palace substructures the cellars survive because they were filled with rubbish for centuries; they map the imperial floor plan above exactly. walk

motovun a walled hill town over a truffle forest, with a walkable rampart and a view of the whole mirna valley. truffle hunting in the motovun forest with dogs, october and november the parenzana, a disused railway turned cycle path istrian malvazija from cellars in the villages below food wine history croatia istria & kvarner
inland croatia zagreb's austro-hungarian centre, and the lakes and waterfalls of the karst interior. nature cities architecture

zagreb a central european capital of coffee terraces and museums, with almost nothing mediterranean about it. the museum of broken relationships, which is much better than the joke dolac market above the main square the upper town, and the gas lamps still lit by hand each evening cities art food architecture croatia inland croatia

plitvice lakes sixteen terraced lakes falling into each other over travertine barriers that are still growing. boardwalks directly over the water — swimming is banned and enforced the upper lakes, which most day visitors miss first entry of the day, in autumn, with the mist on the water nature mountains croatia inland croatia

cyprus republic of cyprus nicosia the last divided capital in europe, on an island of byzantine churches and mountain wine. cyprus is the third-largest mediterranean island and has been divided since 1974, with a un buffer zone running through the middle of nicosia. the republic controls the south; the north is administered separately and recognised only by türkiye. beyond the politics, it holds painted byzantine churches in the troodos mountains, roman mosaics at paphos, and one of the oldest wine traditions in the world. history coast sacred wine mountains food
nicosia & the south coast the divided capital inland, and the roman and hellenistic coast west of limassol. history coast food

nicosia a venetian star-shaped fortress city with a un buffer zone through the middle and a crossing on the main shopping street. the venetian walls, eleven bastions, still tracing the city the cyprus museum's neolithic and bronze age collections the ledra street crossing, and the shuttered street either side of it history food cities cyprus nicosia & the south coast
the green line, walked sandbags, oil drums and 1974 shopfronts, visible from the streets that dead-end into them. sobering and entirely ordinary to residents. walk

paphos a harbour town with roman villa floors that are among the finest mosaics anywhere, and royal tombs cut into the rock. the house of dionysos and its mosaic floors tombs of the kings, hellenistic and underground the akamas peninsula's empty beaches, north history coast art cyprus nicosia & the south coast
the troodos mountains painted churches under wooden roofs, vineyards at 1,000 metres, and forest above them. sacred wine mountains nature

omodos & the wine villages cobbled mountain villages growing indigenous grapes nobody else has, around a 12th-century monastery. xynisteri and mavro, grape varieties grown almost nowhere else the painted churches of the troodos, ten of them unesco-listed commandaria, documented since the crusades wine sacred mountains food cyprus the troodos mountains
the barn-roofed painted churches small stone chapels under enormous pitched roofs, frescoed inside floor to ceiling; several need a key fetched from a village house. sacred

czechia czech republic prague the most beautiful city in central europe, and a country that drinks more beer per head than any other. bohemia and moravia were the industrial heart of the habsburg empire and came through the twentieth century with their architecture largely intact — prague was not bombed. outside it, spa towns, sandstone rock cities, moravian vineyards and a chateau in every second valley go almost unvisited. beer is a food group here and has been brewed in plzeň since 1842. architecture history food music nature wine
prague & bohemia the capital on its river, spa towns to the west, and sandstone rock towns to the north. architecture history music nature

prague romanesque, gothic, baroque and cubist stacked on top of each other, with a castle above and a bridge in between. charles bridge at six in the morning — genuinely worth the alarm the castle complex and st vitus's stained glass by mucha vyšehrad, the other castle, with almost nobody on it a pub where they draw a mlíko, a glass of pure foam, and mean it architecture history music food cities czechia prague & bohemia

vyšehrad and the river bend the city's first castle, a cemetery of composers, and the whole of prague from the ramparts without a crowd. walk

český krumlov a castle town in a tight loop of the vltava, essentially unchanged since the 18th century. the baroque theatre, with original 1766 machinery still working the bear moat, which has had bears since the 1700s canoeing the river loop around the town architecture history nature czechia prague & bohemia

český ráj (turnov) 'bohemian paradise': sandstone towers, rock cities and castles on pinnacles, ninety minutes from prague. prachovské skály's maze of rock corridors trosky castle on two volcanic plugs sandstone climbing where the rules ban metal protection nature mountains history czechia prague & bohemia
moravia the eastern half: vineyards, an astronomical clock nobody queues for, and a functionalist villa that changed architecture. wine architecture food

brno czechia's second city: student, modernist and self-deprecating, with an ossuary of 50,000 under the square. villa tugendhat, mies van der rohe, 1930, bookable in advance only the second-largest ossuary in europe, found in 2001 a cannonball fired at 11 am, which is why the cathedral rings noon an hour early architecture food history music czechia moravia

mikulov a chateau town on the austrian border, surrounded by the country's best vineyards and a limestone ridge. wine cellars cut into the rock, open at harvest the jewish quarter and cemetery, one of central europe's most important pálava's limestone hills and their orchids wine nature history czechia moravia
a moravian cellar at harvest burčák — half-fermented, cloudy and briefly available each september — is drunk cold from the barrel and does not travel. cellar

denmark kingdom of denmark copenhagen small, flat, bicycled, and disproportionately good at deciding how things should look. denmark is a peninsula and four hundred islands, none of them far from the sea and none of them high. what it lacks in landscape it returns in design, food and a kind of practised ease — the country invented a word for it and then exported the word. everything is close: you can cross the whole country by train in four hours. design food coast cities history islands
zealand & copenhagen the eastern island: the capital, the royal castles, and a coast of white cliffs. cities design history coast

copenhagen a harbour city clean enough to swim in the middle of, with the densest good eating in the nordics. harbour baths at islands brygge — municipal swimming in the harbour designmuseum danmark and the chairs everyone else copied torvehallerne and the bakeries of nørrebro tivoli after dark, which is better than its reputation design food cities architecture music denmark zealand & copenhagen
swim in the harbour free, supervised in summer, and the result of thirty years of cleaning up a working port. water

estonia republic of estonia tallinn a medieval hanseatic capital run by the most digital state in europe. estonia is closer to finland than to its baltic neighbours in language and temperament, and closer to nobody at all in how thoroughly it moved government online. half the country is forest, a fifth is bog, and the whole coast is shallow, islanded and quiet. it sang its way out of occupation in 1988, and the choral festival that did it still fills a stadium every five years. history architecture nature design music

finland republic of finland helsinki forest, lake, sauna, silence — and a design tradition that came out of all four. finland is 188,000 lakes and more forest per person than anywhere in europe, arranged around a habit of not talking unnecessarily. the sauna is not a spa treatment here; it is where the country conducts its private life, and there are more saunas than cars. lapland in winter is the reason most people come, and the lake district in july is the reason some come back. nature design winter islands food

inari the centre of sámi finland, on a lake with three thousand islands. siida: the sámi museum, written by sámi people ukonsaari, a sacred island out on the lake aurora with almost no light pollution in any direction winter nature history finland finnish lapland
siida, on sámi terms a national minority telling its own story, including the parts about the finnish state — worth an afternoon rather than an hour. museum

france french republic paris the most visited country on earth, and still mostly empty fifty kilometres from anywhere famous. france is the size of texas with every landscape europe offers: atlantic surf, alpine glacier, mediterranean cliff, volcanic upland and four hundred kilometres of vineyard between them. it receives more visitors than any country in the world, and almost all of them go to the same six places — which leaves the auvergne, the jura, the aveyron and half of brittany to whoever bothers. food and wine are not a sector here; they are the organising principle. food wine art history architecture mountains coast sacred
paris & île-de-france the capital and the palaces and cathedrals within an hour of it. art architecture food cities sacred

paris nineteenth-century town planning at monumental scale, with the world's densest concentration of art inside it. the musée d'orsay in a railway station, better than the louvre for a single visit père lachaise, a walled city of the dead with its own map the covered passages of the 2nd, from the 1820s a market street — rue mouffetard, rue des martyrs — early on a sunday art architecture food cities wine france paris & île-de-france
a market street before ten cheese, bread, a rotisserie chicken and a bottle, then eat it in a park; the most parisian thing available and it costs almost nothing. table
the covered passages glass-roofed arcades built before the department store and mostly forgotten since — a two-hour walk in the dry. walk

chartres the most complete gothic cathedral in france, with 172 windows of 12th-century glass that survived two wars in boxes. the blue of the notre-dame de la belle-verrière window the labyrinth in the nave floor, walkable on fridays in summer the old town below, on the river sacred architecture history france paris & île-de-france
normandy & brittany tidal islands, invasion beaches, cider country and a celtic peninsula that faces the atlantic. coast history sacred food

mont-saint-michel an abbey on a rock in a bay with the fastest tides in europe, and a village winding up to it. the abbey at opening or on a night visit, not at noon walking the bay barefoot with a guide, which is the only safe way the tide, which moves faster than a person walks on spring highs sacred coast history architecture france normandy & brittany
cross the bay on foot guided, barefoot, over quicksand and channels; the mount is a different thing entirely when you arrive the medieval way. walk

bayeux & the landing beaches a town that kept its cathedral, its 70-metre embroidery of 1066, and the beaches of 1944 twenty minutes away. the bayeux tapestry, seen slowly with the audio guide omaha and the american cemetery above it arromanches, where the concrete harbour is still in the sea history sacred coast france normandy & brittany

saint-malo a corsair city inside granite ramparts, rebuilt stone by stone after 1944, with a tidal range of twelve metres. the ramparts circuit at high tide, when spray comes over walking to the grand bé island at low water — and watching the clock oysters at cancale, ten kilometres east coast history food france normandy & brittany

amboise & the loire châteaux a royal town on the loire, with leonardo's last house at the top of it and chenonceau downstream. chenonceau, built across the river itself clos lucé, where leonardo died in 1519 cycling the loire à vélo between châteaux, all of it flat history architecture wine france the loire & the southwest

a small saint-émilion cellar skip the classified growths and visit a family making 20,000 bottles; you will taste from the barrel and be told the truth about the vintage. cellar

biarritz & the basque coast atlantic surf, a napoleonic resort, and a food culture that belongs to a nation without a state. surf at the côte des basques, where european surfing started in 1957 pintxos across the border in san sebastián, an hour away espelette peppers drying on house fronts in september coast food wine france the loire & the southwest

arles a roman arena still in use, the rhône delta at the door, and the year van gogh painted two hundred canvases here. the amphitheatre, built in 90 ad and still hosting events the camargue: salt, white horses, flamingos, and a rice crop les rencontres, europe's oldest photography festival, in july history art food france provence & the mediterranean
the camargue from a horse the local white horses are bred to work in water; a half-day gets you into marsh no vehicle reaches. ride

marseille france's oldest city, founded by greeks in 600 bc, mediterranean rather than french in almost every respect. the calanques: white limestone inlets, reachable on foot from the edge of town mucem and the footbridge to the fort bouillabaisse where the fishermen eat, not on the vieux-port strip food coast cities art france provence & the mediterranean
walk into the calanques from luminy to sugiton in ninety minutes; in summer access is capped and booked, which is why the water is still clear. walk

georgia georgia tbilisi eight thousand years of winemaking, its own alphabet, and mountains higher than the alps. georgia has been making wine in buried clay qvevri for eight millennia — the oldest evidence anywhere — and has an alphabet used by no other language. it sits on the southern side of the greater caucasus, with 5,000-metre peaks, and its supra feasting tradition, presided over by a tamada, is a formal institution rather than a party. a council of europe member, and european by most political definitions. wine food mountains sacred history wild

germany federal republic of germany berlin sixteen states that were separate countries within living memory, and still behave like it. germany has no single centre because it was assembled from kingdoms and free cities in 1871, and every one of them kept its own capital, cathedral and beer. that is the country's real pleasure: bavaria and hamburg have less in common than france and spain. berlin is a city of the twentieth century, still visibly working through it; the rhine, the black forest and the baltic coast are all quieter than they deserve. history music art food mountains cities rail architecture
berlin & the east the capital, saxony's baroque cities, and the landscape of a country that was two countries. history art music architecture

greece hellenic republic athens six thousand islands, of which two hundred and twenty-seven are inhabited, and a mainland almost nobody visits. greece is more mountain than island by area, and the mainland — epirus, the pindus, the peloponnese — is emptier and greener than the postcards suggest. the islands divide into groups with different architecture, food and weather; the cyclades are white and windy, the ionians green, the dodecanese medieval. everything closes down in the afternoon heat and reopens at six, which is not laziness but sense. islands coast history sacred food mountains wine

hungary hungary budapest a thermal-water capital on the danube, a language related to almost nothing, and sweet wine that outlived empires. hungary sits on a plain of hot springs — budapest alone has over a hundred, and the bathing culture runs from roman to ottoman to imperial. the language is finno-ugric and unrelated to any neighbour, which has shaped a certain separateness. beyond the capital there is lake balaton, the volcanic wine hills above it, and tokaj, where botrytised wine was made a century before sauternes. architecture food wine music history cities

a mouldy cellar in tokaj the black fungus on the walls regulates humidity and is left alone deliberately; taste dry furmint first and six-puttonyos last. cellar

iceland republic of iceland reykjavík a geological work in progress, with a literary tradition older than most european states. iceland sits on the seam between two continental plates, which is why it steams, erupts and rearranges itself. three hundred and eighty thousand people live around the edge; the interior is uninhabited and closed by snow for most of the year. the sagas were written here in the 13th century and the language has changed so little that schoolchildren still read them. nature mountains coast wild history

húsavík a wooden church, a whale museum, and the most reliable whale watching in europe. humpbacks in skjálfandi bay, april to october the whale museum, built by the people who stopped hunting them geosea's cliff-top seawater baths wild coast iceland the westfjords & north

rows.t: whales from an old oak boat the refitted fishing schooners cut their engines and drift; the silence is half of what you came for. wild

ireland ireland dublin a small wet island that exported its writers, its music and a third of its people, and kept the landscape. ireland is green because it rains, and the rain arrives from the atlantic in bands with sun between them. the west is the draw: limestone pavement, sea cliffs, a language still spoken daily, and traditional music played in pubs for the players rather than the audience. dublin is small for a capital and dense with literary ghosts. coast music history nature sacred
dublin & the east the capital, its literature, and a monastic valley in the mountains behind it. cities history music sacred

dublin georgian squares, a 1,200-year-old river crossing, and four nobel laureates in literature from one small city. the book of kells and the long room at trinity kilmainham gaol, where the 1916 leaders were executed the national gallery and the hugh lane, both free a session in the cobblestone rather than temple bar cities history music food art ireland dublin & the east

rows.n: A real session, not a show
rows.t: a real session, not a show musicians sit in a circle facing each other, not the room; the etiquette is quiet during tunes and buy the round. stage

glendalough a 6th-century monastic city in a glacial valley with two lakes, an hour from dublin. the round tower, 30 metres, built as a bell tower and a refuge the spinc ridge walk above the upper lake early morning, before the coaches from dublin sacred nature history ireland dublin & the east
the west & the atlantic galway, the burren's limestone, the aran islands and the cliffs. coast music nature islands

galway a small port city that plays music every night of the week and treats a festival as its natural state. music in the latin quarter, from about nine oysters and guinness at a bar that shucks them in front of you the salthill prom walk, and kicking the wall at the end music food coast cities ireland the west & the atlantic
oysters at the counter native flat oysters from the bay outside, september to april; a dozen, brown bread, and no ceremony. table

the aran islands (inis mór) three limestone islands where irish is the daily language and stone walls divide fields the size of rooms. dún aonghasa, a prehistoric fort on an 87-metre cliff with no railing 1,600 km of dry stone wall on an island 14 km long bicycles, because there is almost nothing else islands history nature coast ireland the west & the atlantic
the island by bicycle hire at the pier, ride the length of it, and be back for the last ferry — the island's whole scale in one day. ride

dingle a fishing town on a peninsula of beehive huts, empty beaches and the westernmost point of europe's mainland fringe. the slea head drive, and stopping at the clocháin gallarus oratory, dry-stone and watertight after 1,200 years music in pubs that are also hardware shops coast music food sacred ireland the west & the atlantic

italy italian republic rome a country invented in 1861 out of places that still think of themselves first. italy holds more unesco world heritage sites than any other country and treats most of them as ordinary streets. it became one state only in 1861, and the food, dialect and civic pride still change every forty kilometres — the pasta shape tells you where you are. the alps in the north are as serious as switzerland's; the south is greek, arab and norman by turns. food wine art architecture history coast mountains sacred
rome & lazio three thousand years stacked vertically, and the hill towns and lakes around it. history sacred art food

rome a city where an insurance office sits on a temple and nobody comments, with the best street-level food in italy. the pantheon, entered free, still roofed by the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built the forum and palatine early, before the heat and the groups testaccio market and the quinto quarto cooking around it borghese gallery, two hours, booked, and worth restructuring a day for history sacred art food cities italy rome & lazio
testaccio, where rome eats the market and the streets around it are where roman offal cooking survives; go at one, order what the sign says. table

rows.n: The Appian Way on a Sunday
rows.t: the appian way on a sunday the road is closed to traffic on sundays: basalt paving from 312 bc, catacombs, aqueducts and countryside, inside the city. walk

orvieto a town on a plug of volcanic rock with a striped cathedral and an etruscan city tunnelled underneath it. the cathedral facade, and signorelli's apocalypse frescoes inside st patrick's well: a double-helix staircase 54 metres down 1,200 caves cut into the tufa beneath the streets architecture wine history sacred italy rome & lazio
tuscany & the centre the renaissance where it happened, plus siena's rivalry and the hill towns between. art wine architecture food

florence a banking city that funded the renaissance and kept nearly all of it inside a twenty-minute walk. brunelleschi's dome, climbed at opening the uffizi, booked, and the bargello, which is empty and holds the sculpture san miniato al monte at vespers, with the monks singing bistecca alla fiorentina, which is a cut and a thickness, not a doneness art architecture food wine italy tuscany & the centre
vespers at san miniato gregorian chant in an 11th-century church above the city, at 17:30, free, and almost always uncrowded. sacred

siena a medieval city that lost to florence and was preserved by losing, arranged around a shell-shaped square. the campo, and the palio run around it twice each summer the cathedral's inlaid marble floor, uncovered a few weeks a year the contrade — seventeen districts with their own churches, museums and feuds history architecture art food italy tuscany & the centre

bologna forty kilometres of porticoes, the oldest university in the world, and the best eating in italy. the quadrilatero's food shops, unchanged in layout since the middle ages portico di san luca: 666 arches uphill to a basilica tagliatelle al ragù, which is what the world calls bolognese and is not the same thing food history architecture music italy tuscany & the centre
the 666 arches to san luca four kilometres of covered walkway climbing out of the city, built so a procession would never get wet. walk
the north & the dolomites venice and its lagoon, milan's money, the lakes, and limestone towers on the austrian border. architecture mountains design wine winter

venice a city on wooden piles in a lagoon, with no roads, fewer than 50,000 residents left, and no equivalent anywhere. cannaregio and castello, where people still live the accademia and the punta della dogana at opposite ends of taste a traghetto across the grand canal, standing, for two euros torcello and the mosaics that predate the city architecture art history coast italy the north & the dolomites
cicchetti and an ombra small plates and a small glass of wine at a bàcaro, standing, moving on after one — the venetian version of an aperitivo. table

ortisei & the dolomites pale limestone towers over alpine meadows, in a valley where ladin is still the first language. alpe di siusi, the largest high-altitude meadow in europe via ferrata routes built by soldiers in 1915–18 rifugi serving south tyrolean food at 2,000 metres mountains winter nature food italy the north & the dolomites
a night in a rifugio dinner at seven, lights out at ten, and the enrosadira — the pink glow on the rock at dawn — from the door. walk

milan italy's working city: fashion, design, finance, and a last supper that has to be booked months ahead. the duomo roof terraces, walked among the spires leonardo's last supper, fifteen minutes, booked in advance navigli canals at aperitivo hour design art food cities italy the north & the dolomites
the south & the islands naples, pompeii, the puglian heel, and sicily's greek temples under an active volcano. food history coast islands wine

naples loud, dense, greek in origin, with the best pizza and the best archaeological museum in the world. the archaeological museum, which holds everything good from pompeii pizza in a room with a wood oven and four tables naples underground: greek quarries, aqueducts and war shelters pompeii and herculaneum, twenty minutes by local train food history art coast italy the south & the islands
fried pizza on the street older and poorer than the baked kind, folded into a wallet and eaten walking; the sign to look for is a queue of locals. table

matera cave dwellings inhabited for nine thousand years, evacuated in 1952 as a national disgrace, now a unesco site. the sassi, and rock churches with byzantine frescoes a restored cave house showing how families and animals shared one room the gorge opposite, and the view back at night history architecture food italy the south & the islands

palermo norman, arab and byzantine in the same building, with the best street food in italy underneath. the cappella palatina: islamic ceiling, byzantine mosaics, norman king ballarò and capo markets, shouted rather than sold monreale's mosaics, twenty minutes uphill food history architecture sacred italy the south & the islands
palermo by street food panelle, arancine, sfincione, and — if you are brave — pani ca meusa. a thousand years of occupation in six snacks. table

syracuse & ortigia once the most powerful greek city in the world, now an island old town with a doric temple inside the cathedral. the cathedral, built inside a 5th-century bc temple, columns and all the greek theatre, still used for classical drama each summer swimming off the rocks at the tip of ortigia at sunset history coast food sacred italy the south & the islands

kosovo republic of kosovo pristina europe's youngest country by both age and population, with medieval monasteries and a mountain trail into two neighbours. kosovo declared independence in 2008 and is recognised by around half the world's states, not including serbia — a fact that shapes travel logistics more than daily experience. it is the youngest population in europe, with an energetic café culture in pristina, four unesco-listed serbian orthodox monasteries, and a share of the peaks of the balkans trail through the accursed mountains. history sacred mountains food nature
pristina & the plain the young capital and the historic battlefield plain around it. history food cities

pristina a capital of cafés, brutalist landmarks and a median age under thirty. the national library, which everyone has an opinion about newborn, the typographic monument repainted every year gračanica monastery, 14th-century frescoes, ten minutes out history food cities art kosovo pristina & the plain
prizren & the mountains the ottoman city under a fortress, and the rugova valley into the accursed mountains. history sacred mountains nature

prizren a river town of mosques, orthodox churches and a stone bridge, under a fortress with the whole valley below it. sinan pasha mosque and the church of our lady of ljeviš, on the same street the fortress at sunset, walked up in twenty minutes dokufest, when films are screened on the river and in the castle history sacred architecture food kosovo prizren & the mountains
up to kaljaja at sunset twenty minutes of steps for the whole town, its minarets and its bell towers in one frame. walk

peja & rugova a bazaar town at the mouth of a limestone gorge, with a patriarchate monastery and the accursed mountains behind. the patriarchate of peć, a unesco site and the seat of the serbian church rugova canyon, and via ferrata routes in it the peaks of the balkans trail, crossing into montenegro and albania mountains sacred nature wild kosovo prizren & the mountains

latvia republic of latvia riga the largest collection of art nouveau in europe, on the edge of a great pine forest. latvia's capital was one of the baltic's richest ports in 1900, and it spent the money on facades — whole streets of them, with faces and peacocks and screaming stone masks. outside riga the country is forest, river and a long white beach, and the folk song tradition is enormous: over a million texts collected, and a festival that fills a stadium to sing them. architecture art nature music coast
riga & around the capital, its art nouveau quarter, a beach resort down the line and a castle valley up it. architecture art coast cities

riga a hanseatic old town wrapped in a boulevard ring, wrapped in the best art nouveau streets in europe. alberta iela, where mikhail eisenstein put faces on every facade the central market in five zeppelin hangars the wooden architecture of kalnciema across the river the latvian national museum of art, sharp and well-lit architecture art cities food music latvia riga & around
the facades of alberta iela ninety minutes and a raised chin: everything worth seeing here is above the first floor. walk
lunch in the zeppelin hangars smoked fish, black bread, curd and pickles bought from four different counters and eaten standing up. table

sigulda three castles above a sandstone river gorge, an hour from riga by train. turaida's red brick castle above the gauja gūtmanis cave, carved with visitors' names since the 1600s the bobsleigh track, open to the public in winter nature history latvia riga & around
kurzeme & the coast the western province: empty white beaches, a soviet ghost town, and liepāja's wind. coast history music

liepāja a wind-blown port with a derelict tsarist naval town at its northern end and a rock music habit. karosta: a russian imperial naval base, half-ruined, still lived in the northern forts collapsing into the sea seven kilometres of empty beach coast history music latvia kurzeme & the coast

kuldīga a wooden town on europe's widest waterfall, which is only two metres high but 249 metres across. ventas rumba, where fish jump the falls in spring latvia's longest brick bridge, from 1874 timber streets almost untouched since the 18th century history nature latvia kurzeme & the coast

liechtenstein principality of liechtenstein vaduz twenty-five kilometres long, ruled from a castle on the hill, and walkable end to end in a day. liechtenstein has 40,000 people, no airport, no army, and more registered companies than citizens. it uses the swiss franc, shares switzerland's customs and is in the eea but not the eu. for a visitor it is a mountain principality with an excellent modern art museum, a princely wine cellar, and a hiking trail that crosses the whole country. mountains art wine nature
the rhine valley & the mountains vaduz on the valley floor, and the ski village of malbun in a bowl above it. art mountains wine nature

rows.t: vaduz a capital of 5,700 people under a castle the prince actually lives in, with a black concrete art museum on the main street. kunstmuseum liechtenstein and the princely collections the vineyard walk below the castle walking up to the castle gate, which is as close as anyone gets art wine mountains liechtenstein the rhine valley & the mountains

lithuania republic of lithuania vilnius a baroque capital, a sand spit shared with russia, and a hill of a hundred thousand crosses. lithuania was once the largest state in europe, and the memory of it sits oddly on a country of under three million. vilnius has the biggest baroque old town in the region, full of courtyards you walk into by accident. the curonian spit is a 98-kilometre dune of shifting sand, and the hill of crosses is one of the strangest and most moving places on the continent. history sacred architecture coast nature
vilnius & the east the baroque capital, an artists' republic across a bridge, and a lake castle an hour away. history architecture sacred cities

vilnius forty churches, endless courtyards, and a self-declared republic of artists over the river. st anne's, which napoleon reportedly wanted to carry to paris the gate of dawn and its silver icon, still a pilgrimage užupis, its constitution and its angel the kgb museum in the building where it happened architecture sacred history cities art lithuania vilnius & the east
the courtyards nobody signposts the old town's real geography is behind the street doors; push the unlocked ones and keep going. walk
read the užupis constitution forty-one articles on mirrored plaques, including a dog's right to be a dog and everyone's right to be happy — and not to be. walk

trakai a red brick island castle in a lake, and the karaim community that has lived beside it since the 14th century. the island castle, reachable by footbridge kibinai pastries in karaim wooden houses rowing boats and swimming in the same lake history nature food lithuania vilnius & the east
the coast & centre the curonian dunes, the port at klaipėda, and the hill outside šiauliai. coast sacred nature

nida, curonian spit wooden fishermen's houses under a moving dune, on a sand spit between lagoon and sea. parnidis dune and its sundial, with the russian border visible south thomas mann's summer house, where he wrote in 1930–32 amber, smoked fish, and no cars to speak of coast nature islands lithuania the coast & centre

rows.n: The grey dunes at first light
rows.t: the grey dunes at first light sand that buried four villages in the 19th century; the boardwalk exists because walking on it directly would start it moving again. walk

šiauliai an industrial town whose reason to visit stands in a field twelve kilometres north. the hill of crosses: over 100,000 crosses, bulldozed three times by the soviets and rebuilt each night the sound the small crosses make in wind a cathedral with a sundial column sacred history lithuania the coast & centre
the hill of crosses not a monument — an act repeated by hundreds of thousands of people, most of them anonymous, over two centuries. sacred

luxembourg grand duchy of luxembourg luxembourg city a fortress city on a gorge, a wine river, and free public transport across the whole country. luxembourg is 2,586 square kilometres, trilingual by default, and richer per head than almost anywhere. the capital sits on a rock split by two river valleys, with casemates tunnelled through it. in 2020 it made all public transport free nationwide, which turns out to be the single best reason to travel around it slowly. history wine nature architecture
the capital & the moselle the fortress city, and the vineyard river that forms the german border. history wine architecture

luxembourg city a unesco-listed fortress on cliffs, with 17 kilometres of tunnels underneath and a modern quarter on the plateau above. the bock casemates, cut into the rock from 1644 the chemin de la corniche, called europe's most beautiful balcony the grund at the bottom of the gorge, reached by a free lift history architecture cities luxembourg the capital & the moselle
into the bock casemates kilometres of gun galleries in the cliff; they sheltered 35,000 people in 1944 and are cold in any weather. walk

remich & the moselle terraced vineyards on a slow river, with germany on the far bank and crémant cellars on this one. crémant tasting where it is bottled the riverside cycle path along both banks harvest weekends in late september wine nature food luxembourg the capital & the moselle
mullerthal & the ardennes sandstone ravines in the east, and castle country in the wooded north. nature history mountains

echternach the country's oldest town, with a 7th-century abbey and a hopping procession on the unesco list. the mullerthal trail through sandstone clefts and moss the basilica and its crypt the dancing procession, every whit tuesday since the middle ages sacred nature history luxembourg mullerthal & the ardennes
little switzerland on foot 112 km of waymarked trail through gorges narrow enough to touch both walls; a day section is easy and free. walk

vianden a restored hilltop castle above a river village, where victor hugo spent his exile. the castle, one of the largest west of the rhine hugo's house on the bridge, kept as it was the chairlift up for the view back history nature luxembourg mullerthal & the ardennes

malta republic of malta valletta three inhabited islands of limestone, holding temples older than the pyramids and a city built by knights. malta is 316 square kilometres, the most densely populated country in the eu, and has been fought over by everyone with a navy since the bronze age. its megalithic temples predate stonehenge and giza. valletta was built from scratch in the 1560s as a fortress city and is still walkable in twenty minutes. english is an official language, which makes it unusually easy going. history coast architecture sacred islands
malta the main island: the fortress capital, the old silent city, and the temples on the southern cliffs. history architecture sacred coast

valletta a planned fortress city of 1566, on a peninsula between two harbours, with caravaggio's largest painting in its cathedral. st john's co-cathedral, plain outside and overwhelming inside caravaggio's beheading of st john, the only work he signed the upper barrakka gardens and the noon gun over the grand harbour the three cities across the water, by traditional dgħajsa boat history architecture art coast malta malta

rows.n: Across the Grand Harbour by dgħajsa
rows.t: across the grand harbour by dgħajsa a rowed and now motorised water taxi in the old harbour shape; the cheapest and best view of the bastions. water

mdina & rabat the old walled capital on a hill, with about 250 residents and no traffic — called the silent city for a reason. the bastion walls over the whole island at dusk st paul's catacombs, cut in the 3rd century evening, when the day visitors leave and it earns its name history architecture sacred malta malta

ħaġar qim & the south cliffs megalithic temples on a cliff over the sea, built between 3600 and 3200 bc. some of the oldest free-standing structures on earth the solstice alignment through a small oval port the blue grotto below, by boat in calm weather history sacred coast malta malta
gozo & comino the green sister island, slower and more agricultural, with a neolithic temple and a lagoon. islands coast history nature

victoria, gozo a citadel town in the middle of an island where the pace drops noticeably the moment the ferry docks. the ċittadella walls, and the whole island visible from them ġgantija: temples older than ħaġar qim, and older than the pyramids salt pans at xwejni, cut into the rock and still worked by one family islands history coast food malta gozo & comino
the xwejni salt pans rock-cut pans worked by the same family for five generations; they harvest by hand in summer and will explain it if you ask. workshop

moldova republic of moldova chișinău the world's largest wine cellar, measured in kilometres, under one of europe's least visited countries. moldova is small, agricultural and almost entirely overlooked, which is precisely the argument for going. it has been making wine for five thousand years and stores it in limestone mines: mileștii mici holds two million bottles in 200 kilometres of tunnel. a cave monastery is cut into a cliff over the răut, and rural guesthouse tourism is genuinely community-run. wine food sacred nature history
chișinău & the cellars the capital, and the underground wine cities within an hour of it. wine food cities

chișinău a green, low-rise capital of parks and soviet-era planning, with the wine country immediately outside it. cricova and mileștii mici, driven through by car the central market, and the produce of a country that mostly farms soviet mosaics and modernist buildings on the edges wine food cities moldova chișinău & the cellars
driving through a wine cellar 200 km of limestone galleries with street names, and two million bottles. visitors go in by vehicle because walking would take days. cellar
orheiul vechi & the north a cave monastery above a river meander, and the villages around it. sacred nature history

orheiul vechi a monastery dug into a limestone cliff over a loop of the răut, inhabited on and off since the 13th century. the cave church, reached along the cliff edge butuceni village below, with guesthouses in stone houses getic and tatar remains in the same valley sacred nature history moldova orheiul vechi & the north

monaco principality of monaco monaco two square kilometres of rock, casino and grand prix circuit, wedged between france and the sea. monaco is the second-smallest country in the world and the most densely populated, built vertically up a cliff because there is nowhere else to go. it is not in the eu or schengen in its own right, though you enter through france and will not notice a border. for a visitor it is a half-day: the old town on the rock, the casino, the harbour, and the fact that a formula one circuit runs through all three. coast architecture cities art
the rock & the harbour the old town on its promontory, the port below, and monte-carlo along the bay. coast architecture art cities

monaco-ville the medieval quarter on the rock: palace, cathedral, and an oceanographic museum built into the cliff face. the oceanographic museum, founded by a prince who was a serious scientist the changing of the guard at 11:55, briskly the exotic garden and the cave beneath it history coast architecture monaco the rock & the harbour
walk the grand prix circuit 3.3 km of ordinary public road: the tunnel, the hairpin, the harbour chicane. it takes forty minutes and recalibrates what you think those cars are doing. walk

montenegro montenegro podgorica a drowned river canyon that looks like a fjord, with black mountains straight up behind it. montenegro is smaller than wales and rises from sea level to 2,500 metres within twenty kilometres. the bay of kotor is a ria — a flooded river valley — walled by cliffs, with venetian towns around its edge. behind it, durmitor's plateau and the tara canyon are properly wild. it uses the euro without being in the eu or the eurozone formally. coast mountains history nature

rows.n: The Bay of Kotor & the Coast

rows.t: kotor a walled venetian town at the head of the bay, with fortifications climbing 260 metres up the cliff behind it. the 1,350 steps up the fortress walls, at dawn before the heat the old town's cats, which have their own museum our lady of the rocks, an artificial island built by sailors dropping stones coast history mountains architecture montenegro the bay of kotor & the coast
the city walls at dawn ninety minutes up, the whole bay below, and a small church halfway. go before eight or don't go in july. walk

durmitor & the north a high limestone plateau, glacial lakes, and the second-deepest canyon in the world. mountains nature wild

žabljak the highest town in the balkans at 1,450 metres, at the edge of durmitor national park. the black lake, twenty minutes' walk from the town bobotov kuk, 2,523 metres, a long day on rock the tara canyon, 1,300 metres deep, rafted in spring mountains nature winter wild montenegro durmitor & the north
rafting the tara the deepest canyon in europe, drinkable water the whole way, and a season from may to october. water

netherlands kingdom of the netherlands amsterdam a country built on purpose, mostly below sea level, and cycled end to end. a quarter of the netherlands lies below sea level and nearly all of it was arranged by people — drained, diked, pumped and planned. that habit of design runs through the painting, the cities and the bicycle infrastructure, which is the best on earth and not close. amsterdam absorbs most visitors; utrecht, rotterdam and the northern islands absorb almost none. art design architecture cities food
the randstad the dense western ring: amsterdam, rotterdam, the hague, utrecht and the polder between them. art architecture cities design

amsterdam a 17th-century canal plan that still works, with two of the world's great collections inside it. the rijksmuseum, and half an hour in front of the vermeers the van gogh museum, booked ahead or not at all the jordaan and the nine streets on foot a canal at seven in the morning, before the boats art architecture cities food music netherlands the randstad

rotterdam flattened in 1940 and rebuilt as an argument for modern architecture, on europe's largest port. the markthal, a food market inside a housing block depot boijmans, the first publicly accessible art storage building anywhere harbour tours through a port that runs for forty kilometres architecture design cities food netherlands the randstad

utrecht amsterdam's canals at half the scale and a fifth of the crowd, with wharf cellars at water level. the oudegracht's two-level canals, unique in europe the dom tower, 112 metres, 465 steps rietveld's schröder house, the built manifesto of de stijl cities food architecture netherlands the randstad
the north & the wadden islands frisian country, mudflats that appear at low tide, and islands with no cars. nature coast islands wild

wadlopen — walking the sea floor guided walks across the exposed seabed at low tide, thigh-deep in mud, timed against a returning sea. never attempted alone. walk

north macedonia republic of north macedonia skopje one of the oldest lakes on earth, a bazaar that never stopped trading, and a capital that rebuilt itself in marble. north macedonia is landlocked, mountainous, and centred on lake ohrid — between three and five million years old, with sixty endemic species and a town of churches on its shore. skopje was flattened by an earthquake in 1963, rebuilt in concrete, and then rebuilt again in the 2010s in a neoclassical style that its own citizens argue about constantly. sacred history nature food mountains
ohrid & the southwest the ancient lake, its churches, and the mountains between here and albania. sacred nature history coast

ohrid a town of byzantine churches on a cliff over one of the world's oldest lakes, with a slavic literary tradition that began here. sveti jovan kaneo, on a cliff over the water the lake itself: 3–5 million years old, 288 metres deep plaošnik, where cyrillic literacy was taught in the 9th century swimming from the town beaches in july and august sacred nature history coast north macedonia ohrid & the southwest

poland republic of poland warsaw a country that was erased from the map for 123 years and rebuilt its capital from paintings. poland is large, flat in the middle, mountainous in the south and forested in the east, where europe's last primeval woodland still stands. its cities carry the twentieth century openly: warsaw was destroyed and reconstructed, kraków survived intact, gdańsk was rebuilt as a hanseatic port. it is one of the best-value countries in europe and the food has become genuinely interesting in the last decade. history food mountains nature sacred cities

arctic to the baltic midnight sun to hanseatic brick start where the sun does not set and end where medieval merchants counted their money. this is the long north: an arctic city, an island chain of granite peaks, a night train down the spine of sweden, and then the three old trading capitals of the baltic — each of which was rich, then occupied, and is now itself again. long legs, and the train is the point rather than the cost.

the alpine grand tour six valleys, four countries, one mountain range the alps are a single range and five nationalities, and the way to feel that is to cross them slowly by train and cable car rather than fly over. this route runs west to east from mont blanc to the dolomites, staying high, and every leg is on a scheduled public service. book the mountain huts before you book the hotels.

scandinavia to central europe copenhagen to budapest, all by rail a north-south line down the middle of the continent, from a harbour you can swim in to a capital built on hot springs. it crosses the old inner-german border, the old iron curtain, and three empires' worth of architecture, without ever needing a flight or a car. the stretch from berlin to budapest is the densest run of great cities in europe.

the adriatic run venice to dubrovnik the long way round down the eastern adriatic, which has the mediterranean's clearest water and its least developed coastline. the route leaves the sea twice on purpose — into slovenia's karst and into bosnia — because the interior is where the layers are: venetian, ottoman, habsburg and yugoslav, sometimes in the same street. ferries and buses, not trains, from split onward.

camino & sacred europe six places people have walked to for a thousand years not a religious journey unless you want it to be — a route through the buildings and landscapes that pilgrimage produced, which is most of what europe built before it built anything else. it ends where it should, on foot, in the rain, in galicia. two of these stops are still working monastic communities and one is a sovereign state.

the hanseatic arc the medieval trading league, in order between the 13th and 17th centuries a network of merchant towns ran the northern seas, and they all built with the same brick and the same confidence. this route follows them from flanders to the gulf of finland. what the league left behind is a very specific pleasure: gabled warehouses, town halls larger than the towns needed, and a shared idea of what a rich city should look like.

the classical mediterranean greek and roman cities, on both shores three thousand years of the same sea. this route takes in the best-preserved classical cities on either side of the mediterranean — a sicilian cathedral built inside a doric temple, a roman arena still hosting events, and the anatolian coast where more of the greek world survives than in greece. two flights or ferries are unavoidable and are worth it.

rows.s: Walls, guilds and the towns that stopped changing
rows.t: medieval europe walls, guilds and the towns that stopped changing a medieval town survives for one of two reasons: it stayed poor, or it stayed useful. these did one or the other. look for the shape rather than the set pieces — a market square where the roads meet, a wall that a rich century paid for, and a church larger than the population ever justified.

rows.s: Where people have gone on purpose for a thousand years
rows.t: sacred europe where people have gone on purpose for a thousand years pilgrimage built more of europe than any king did: the roads, the bridges, the hostels, the towns that grew where walkers stopped. these places span four christian traditions and are all still in use — which means visiting them means visiting somebody's church rather than a monument.

rows.s: Ships, settlements and the places they reached
rows.t: viking europe ships, settlements and the places they reached the norse were traders and settlers more often than raiders, and the archaeology says so: ships built for cargo, parliaments held in the open air, and towns founded from dublin to kyiv. these are the places where you can see the evidence rather than the reputation.

mountain europe eight ranges, one continent europe's mountains are not one thing. the alps are high and serviced; the caucasus is higher and barely; the tatras are compressed; the picos end in the sea; the accursed mountains have a blood-feud memory and a trail through three countries. this is the case for treating them as different places rather than one activity.

rows.s: The empire, where it is still standing up
rows.t: roman europe the empire, where it is still standing up rome's best surviving buildings are mostly not in rome. they are in the provinces, where a later city did not need the stone, or where a cathedral was built inside the temple instead of on top of it. these are the places where the engineering is still doing its job.

rows.s: Eight regions that do not taste like each other
rows.t: wine europe eight regions that do not taste like each other the interesting wine map of europe is not the famous one. it includes clay vessels buried in georgian courtyards, volcanic vines woven into baskets against aegean wind, and slate slopes on the rhine at sixty degrees. every one of these places will let you taste in the cellar where it was made.

rows.t: rail europe journeys where the train is the destination some lines were built to move slate, ore or salt and are now worth the fare on their own. others were engineering arguments. all of these are scheduled public services rather than tourist excursions, which means you can use them as transport and get the spectacle for the price of a ticket.

rows.n: Hay meadows and the people who cut them
rows.t: hay meadows and the people who cut them transylvania's hay meadows hold some of the richest plant diversity in europe, and they hold it because they are cut by hand at the right time each year. mechanised cutting destroys them within a decade. scythe blades, peening tools and training weeks, plus a small per-hectare payment that makes hand cutting survivable for families who would otherwise stop.

wooden churches of maramureș shingle-roofed oak churches built without nails, some from the 1600s, in villages of a few hundred people. shingles last about thirty years and the craft of splitting them is held by a handful of people. apprenticeships in shingle splitting, and materials for two roofs a year.

sámi-language media and youth programmes there are ten sámi languages and several have fewer than a thousand speakers. media and youth programming in the language does more for its survival than any monument. production support for sámi-language youth media, and residential language weeks for teenagers.

dry stone walls, inis mór sixteen hundred kilometres of dry stone wall on an island fourteen kilometres long, built to clear the ground and to make soil out of sand and seaweed. they fall down and are rebuilt by hand or not at all. wall-building weeks with island masons, and a small fund for the sections along public paths that visitors damage.

rows.n: Coast path erosion, the Lycian Way
rows.t: coast path erosion, the lycian way 540 kilometres of waymarked path opened in 1999, now carrying far more feet than it was built for, across soft limestone and through villages with no maintenance budget. waymark repainting, drainage work on the eroded sections above kabak, and payment to the village households who maintain the stages nearest them.

lake ohrid endemic species monitoring between three and five million years old, with over sixty species found nowhere else, and under pressure from sewage, water abstraction and shoreline building. monitoring equipment and student stipends, and support for the enforcement of the wild trout ban that restaurants routinely ignore.

rows.n: Guesthouse training in the Albanian Alps
rows.t: guesthouse training in the albanian alps the valbona-theth crossing has gone from almost no visitors to thousands a season within a decade, and the money mostly stays local because the beds are family-run. that is fragile and worth protecting. water and waste systems for village guesthouses, first aid and mountain safety training, and a shared booking system that is not owned by a platform.

sephardic thessaloniki, documented thessaloniki was a majority-sephardic city for four centuries. almost the entire community was deported in 1943. the documentation of what was there is held in fragments across several countries. archival digitisation, translation of ladino material, and school programmes in the city itself.

qvevri makers, kakheti the clay vessels georgian wine ferments in are made by a handful of families. the technique is on the unesco intangible heritage list and the number of working makers is in single figures. apprentice stipends, kiln repair, and a survey of the surviving clay sources.

wadden sea mudflat guiding walking the exposed sea floor at low tide requires a guide who knows the channels and the tide tables, and the licensing and training of those guides is entirely voluntary work. training and licensing costs for new guides, and safety equipment for the routes to ameland and schiermonnikoog.

bear coexistence in the carpathians romania holds most of europe's brown bears. conflict with people rises every year, driven largely by roadside feeding and unsecured rubbish, and the animals lose that argument. bear-proof bins in mountain villages, electric fencing for smallholders' orchards, and the field staff who install both.
